questions.hint: Separate query representation, strategy selection and execution.

evidence.quote: Parsing checks SQL grammar; semantic analysis resolves names, types and access permissions. Translation constructs a logical representation, typically relational algebra or a logical query tree. Optimization chooses equivalent operations, join order and physical access methods. Evaluation executes that plan and returns results. Not every implementation exposes exactly the same phase boundaries.
Query processing is the whole activity; selecting a suitable efficient strategy is optimization.
A query graph represents the predicate relationships of a relational-calculus expression without itself prescribing an operator execution order.

questions.hint: Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary.

evidence.quote: Deferred update keeps uncommitted changes outside the persistent database; in the usual no-force setting it is NO-UNDO/REDO. Redo-only and NO-UNDO/REDO mean the same thing, so those cannot be separate unique answers. Immediate update allows persistent changes before commit and therefore may require undo; it need not flush every write_item immediately.
Shadow/copy-on-write update writes a new location while preserving the committed version.
In-place update overwrites the original location.

questions.editorial_resolution: Replaces an overstrong immediate-flush account with the precommit permission rule in ADB29; answer B is retained.

answer_review.explanation: Immediate update permits a transaction's changes to be written to the persistent database before commit. If that transaction later aborts, recovery may need to undo those changes. Deferred update keeps uncommitted changes outside the persistent database. In-place update describes overwriting an existing location, while shadow update describes writing a separate version. Those location strategies do not, by their names alone, specify the timing policy requested here. Immediate update need not flush every cache write immediately.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Describes overwriting the existing location, not the commit-timing policy.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Correct: immediate update permits persistent database changes before commit and may require undo.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Describes writing a separate version while preserving the committed one, not the requested timing policy.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Deferred update excludes uncommitted changes from the persistent database.

answer_review.explanation: Heuristic optimization uses algebraic rules to reduce intermediate work, for example applying selective filters earlier, replacing a product plus join predicate with a join and projecting away unneeded columns. A practical optimizer can combine rewriting and costing, but the question isolates the rule-based transformation role.

questions.hint: Track the first lock release and the transaction-completion boundary.

evidence.quote: Basic 2PL has a growing phase that acquires/upgrades locks and a shrinking phase that releases/downgrades them. Once any lock is released, no new lock may be acquired. The lock point is the instant the final lock is obtained. 2PL guarantees conflict serializability for well-formed transactions, but can deadlock and basic 2PL alone need not prevent cascading aborts.
Two-phase locking orders access to data; two-phase commit coordinates a distributed commit decision.
Strict 2PL retains exclusive locks until commit/abort.

answer_review.explanation: Two-phase locking acquires locks in the growing phase, then releases them in the shrinking phase without acquiring new ones. (Database System.pdf, PDF pp. 86.)

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Release is the unlocking portion, not acquisition. (PDF pp. 86.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Rollback is not one of the two acquisition/release phases. (PDF pp. 86.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Shrinking forbids new locks. (PDF pp. 86.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Growing allows acquisition and forbids release. (PDF pp. 86.)

questions.hint: Trace which transaction wrote each value and whether an overwrite or mixed-version read occurs.

evidence.quote: Lost update: T1 and T2 both read 500; T2 adds 200 and writes 700; T1 adds 100 to its stale value and writes 600. Correct serial execution yields 800. Dirty read: T2 reads a value written by uncommitted T1; if T1 aborts, dependent work must be reconsidered. Reading one's own changes is not a dirty read.

questions.hint: Distinguish transaction ordering, conflict conditions and full execution equivalence.

evidence.quote: A serial schedule executes each transaction's operations consecutively. A serializable schedule is equivalent to some serial order; it may interleave transactions. Equality of one final value is insufficient evidence because different executions can accidentally coincide. Two operations conflict when they belong to different transactions, access the same item and at least one writes. Read/read pairs do not conflict.

answer_review.explanation: Conflict requires different transactions, the same item, and at least one write. Membership in the same transaction is therefore the exception; the supplied D key reverses the definition. (Database System.pdf, PDF pp. 70, 71.)

choices.label: A

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Same-transaction operations fail the different-transaction requirement. (PDF pp. 70, 71.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: At least one write is required. (PDF pp. 70, 71.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Different transactions is required, so D is not the exception. (PDF pp. 70, 71.)

questions.hint: Identify what failed, what durable resources survive and which restoration action is required.

evidence.quote: Restart recovery restores a valid database after a crash while preserving durable commits and removing incomplete effects. Rollback handles failed/uncommitted work; redo preserves committed work missing from pages; checkpoints reduce log-search work; backups provide another stored copy.
Undo restores before-images of incomplete effects, usually traversing that transaction's updates backward. Redo installs logged after-images when necessary, usually forward.
A view is a stored query definition, not encryption.

questions.editorial_resolution: All alternatives are classified by the positive definitions in ADB26, ADB27, ADB06. The repair replaces source-gap rejection with concrete contrasting rules and states any needed scope.

answer_review.explanation: Atomicity requires removing the effects of an incomplete transaction after a crash. Rollback performs that undo work, restoring before-images as needed. Commit instead accepts successful transaction effects, and a view is a query representation rather than a recovery action. Redo installs logged after-images to recover missing work; it does not name the removal of uncommitted effects requested here. These actions occur during restart recovery after the system is operating again.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Incorrect: a view is not an operation that reverses transaction effects.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Incorrect: commit accepts transaction effects rather than undoing the incomplete work.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Correct: rollback undoes the effects of the uncommitted transaction.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Incorrect: redo installs logged after-images; the requested removal requires undo/rollback.

questions.hint: Distinguish a waiting cycle, a long wait and indefinite unfair postponement.

evidence.quote: Deadlock requires a waiting cycle: T1 holds X and wants Y; T2 holds Y and wants X. In a wait-for graph, an edge Ti→Tj means Ti waits for a lock held by Tj. A cycle indicates deadlock under the ordinary lock-wait model. Abort a suitable victim, undo its effects and release its locks; repeat if other cycles remain. Aborting every deadlocked transaction also breaks cycles but wastes more work.
Fair queues, sensible victim selection and retaining original transaction timestamps on retry reduce starvation; deadlock freedom alone does not prove fairness.
A timeout aborts long waits but may mistake slow progress for deadlock.

answer_review.explanation: Mutual waiting among transactions for locks held by one another is the module's deadlock condition. (Database System.pdf, PDF pp. 87.)

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Idle does not express mutual lock waiting. (PDF pp. 87.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Waiting alone need not involve a cycle. (PDF pp. 87.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Deadlock is mutual waiting that prevents progress. (PDF pp. 87.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Ready does not describe transactions blocked on one another. (PDF pp. 87.)

questions.hint: Identify whether the scenario concerns identity, permission, disclosure or valid values.

evidence.quote: Authentication establishes identity; authorization/access control determines permitted actions. Encryption protects stored or transmitted content; integrity constraints restrict valid data; auditing records actions. A user who can view but cannot change a record has restricted access privileges. A view can restrict visible rows/columns, but its privilege and execution rules must support that restriction.
Inference control concerns learning protected individual facts indirectly from allowed aggregate answers.
Releasing SUM for a group and SUM for the same group excluding one known person may disclose that person's value by subtraction.

answer_review.hint: Identify whether the scenario concerns identity, permission, disclosure or valid values.
answer_review.explanation: Inference control targets learning protected individual facts from aggregate answers. For example, subtracting a sum excluding one person from a sum including that person can reveal their value even when their row is hidden. Ordinary access control grants or denies actions, integrity validates data and encryption protects encoded content. The specified indirect-disclosure threat identifies inference control specifically.

evidence.quote: Fine-grained row locks permit more independent operations but require tracking many locks. Coarse table/database locks simplify management but block unrelated rows and reduce concurrency. Intention locks advertise planned descendant locks in a hierarchy; escalation replaces many small locks with a coarser one. Small granularity does not inherently cause more logical conflicts. Choose granularity from contention and management overhead, not a universal rule.

answer_review.answer_text: Locks with small granularity cause more conflicts.
answer_review.explanation: Fine granularity raises concurrency, whereas coarse granularity locks more data with fewer lock entries. Thus the claim that smaller units cause more conflicts reverses the tradeoff. (Database System.pdf, PDF pp. 83, 95.)

choices.explanation: A single coarse lock can replace many fine locks and reduce management work. (PDF pp. 83, 95.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Fine units allow more independent access, so this is the false claim. (PDF pp. 83, 95.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Coarse locks reduce the number of entries tracked. (PDF pp. 83, 95.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The file/relation granularity in the hierarchy permits table-level locking. (PDF pp. 83, 95.)

choices.label: E
choices.explanation: Entire-database locking is expressly listed. (PDF pp. 83, 95.)

questions.hint: Distinguish an object instance from its class, attribute values and persistent identity.

evidence.quote: An object combines identity, state and behavior. A class specifies the attributes and operations of its instances; an object is one instance. The object identifier (OID) distinguishes objects independently of their attribute values and remains stable over that object's lifetime. Two objects can have equal values and different identities; changing a name does not create a new identity.
It does not primarily present objects as rows and tables.
An object-relational DBMS extends a relational system with richer types; ORM maps programming objects into relational tables.

answer_review.answer_text: The rows-and-tables claim is false for the object-oriented model.
answer_review.hint: Distinguish an object instance from its class, attribute values and persistent identity.
answer_review.explanation: ADB01 distinguishes an OODBMS from relational rows and tables: its primary model is persistent objects with identity, state and behavior. ADB02 supports communication through methods and object references, and ADB03 supports reuse through inheritance. Relational presentation as tables is the contrasting model. Therefore A is the false statement; the source image is not needed to establish that conceptual distinction.

questions.hint: Distinguish completing a transaction from marking an intermediate recovery position.

evidence.quote: In SQL transaction-block notation, BEGIN starts a block, COMMIT completes it successfully, and ROLLBACK cancels its uncommitted changes. Committing requests a durable transaction outcome; it is distinct from merely finishing the last read or write operation.

SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate position inside the current transaction. ROLLBACK TO discards changes made after that position while retaining earlier work in the transaction. A savepoint is not an independent durable commit, and rolling back to it does not itself commit the retained changes.

questions.editorial_resolution: All alternatives are classified by the positive definitions in ADB06, ADB-S02. The repair replaces source-gap rejection with concrete contrasting rules and states any needed scope.

answer_review.explanation: COMMIT successfully completes the transaction and requests a durable committed outcome. ROLLBACK instead cancels uncommitted changes. SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate position to which later work can be rolled back, retaining earlier work within the same transaction; it neither completes that transaction nor makes the retained changes independently durable. Because COMMIT is offered, the none-of-the-choices alternative is false. D therefore identifies the permanent transaction-completion command.

choices.label: A

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Incorrect: COMMIT is offered and is the requested completion command.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Incorrect: SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate rollback position inside the still-open transaction; it does not commit.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Correct: COMMIT completes the transaction successfully and requests a durable outcome.

questions.hint: Distinguish a waiting cycle, a long wait and indefinite unfair postponement.

evidence.quote: Fixed resource ordering and conservative 2PL prevent cycles. A no-wait policy aborts immediately on an incompatible lock request and needs no age timestamp. A timeout aborts long waits but may mistake slow progress for deadlock. Starvation is indefinite postponement while other work proceeds, without a required cycle. Fair queues, sensible victim selection and retaining original transaction timestamps on retry reduce starvation; deadlock freedom alone does not prove fairness.

A smaller timestamp means an older transaction. In wait–die, an older requester may wait for a younger holder; a younger requester needing an older holder aborts itself. In wound–wait, an older requester aborts the younger holder; a younger requester waits for the older holder. Always identify requester versus holder before applying the names.

questions.editorial_resolution: All alternatives are classified by the positive definitions in ADB13, ADB14. The repair replaces source-gap rejection with concrete contrasting rules and states any needed scope.

answer_review.hint: Distinguish a waiting cycle, a long wait and indefinite unfair postponement.
answer_review.explanation: No-wait aborts immediately when a lock request conflicts, so transactions cannot form a lock-wait cycle and no age comparison is needed. Wait–die and wound–wait use relative transaction ages to decide who waits or aborts. Under the explicitly defined wait-wait alternative, every conflicting request may wait without a cycle-prevention restriction, so a transaction can hold one item while waiting for another in a cycle. That alternative therefore fails the deadlock-prevention requirement.

evidence.quote: Fixed resource ordering and conservative 2PL prevent cycles. A no-wait policy aborts immediately on an incompatible lock request and needs no age timestamp. Fair queues, sensible victim selection and retaining original transaction timestamps on retry reduce starvation; deadlock freedom alone does not prove fairness.

A smaller timestamp means an older transaction. In wait–die, an older requester may wait for a younger holder; a younger requester needing an older holder aborts itself. In wound–wait, an older requester aborts the younger holder; a younger requester waits for the older holder. Always identify requester versus holder before applying the names.

choices.label: B

evidence.quote: Full replication places the whole database at every relevant site; partial replication copies selected fragments to selected sites; nonredundant allocation stores each fragment once. Partitioning improves locality and parallelism but alone creates no spare copy.
Flexible schema does not mean no schema rules, and NoSQL does not imply no transactions.

Neither the broader architecture nor a model label specifically says that extra copies are created.

questions.hint: Track durable-write ordering and distinguish reversing incomplete work from installing logged effects.

evidence.quote: Write-ahead logging requires the update log needed for recovery to reach stable storage before the corresponding changed data page reaches disk. To acknowledge a durable commit, force the transaction's required log records, including its commit record, to stable storage. A buffer can be changed before that log flush; WAL orders durable writes, not every CPU assignment.
Undo restores before-images of incomplete effects, usually traversing that transaction's updates backward.
Active transactions can span the checkpoint, so their relevant earlier updates can still need undo.

evidence.quote: Deadlock requires a waiting cycle: T1 holds X and wants Y; T2 holds Y and wants X. In a wait-for graph, an edge Ti→Tj means Ti waits for a lock held by Tj. evidence.quote: Basic 2PL has a growing phase that acquires/upgrades locks and a shrinking phase that releases/downgrades them. Once any lock is released, no new lock may be acquired. Two-phase locking orders access to data; two-phase commit coordinates a distributed commit decision.
Optimistic/validation control reads and computes privately, validates its read/write sets against overlapping transactions, then publishes if validation succeeds; otherwise it retries.

Commit is a transaction event, validation belongs to optimistic control and shrinking has the opposite lock-release role.

questions.hint: Identify which history a recovery boundary can safely exclude and whether active work spans it.

evidence.quote: A checkpoint records enough durable recovery state to avoid scanning all old history. A nondeterministic pushdown automaton (PDA) adds a stack to finite control: (Q,Σ,Γ,δ,q₀,Z₀,F). Its transition relation maps (state,input symbol or ε,stack top) to possible (new state,replacement stack string) pairs.

A stack is last-in, first-out: push adds an item at the top and pop removes the top item, so the most recently pushed item is removed first. A PDA accesses this top rather than an arbitrary interior position.

A queue is first-in, first-out: insertion at the rear and removal at the front returns the oldest waiting item. A linked list can implement a storage discipline, but the implementation container is different from the abstract push/pop or enqueue/dequeue access rule.

Thus every CSL is decidable.

If L is context-free, some p ensures each sufficiently long s∈L has s=uvxyz with |vxy|≤p, |vy|≥1 and uvⁱxyⁱz∈L for every i≥0. The two pieces v and y are pumped together; either may be empty, not both. A non-CFL proof must defeat every allowed decomposition.

For s=aᵖbᵖcᵖ, the window vxy cannot contain both an a and a c. Pumping affects at most two blocks and at least one count. Use i=0 or 2: the unaffected third block retains p while another count changes, or symbol order breaks. Hence aⁿbⁿcⁿ is not CFL.

A decider halts on every input and accepts exactly its language; these languages are recursive/decidable. A recognizer must halt and accept every member, but on a nonmember may halt-reject or loop. Its languages are recursively enumerable (RE), Turing-recognizable or semidecidable. Looping is nonacceptance, not a rejecting halt. An undecidable language may still have a recognizer.
Every decidable language is RE, and the containment is strict.
Finite automata have finite memory encoded by states, not no state or no ability to remember any history.

answer_review.explanation: A recognizer whose memory is a fixed finite state has regular-language power. Every regular language is context-free, so a context-free grammar can also describe its language. The reverse inclusion fails: equal-count matching such as {0^n1^n} is context-free but not regular. Context-sensitive languages need not be regular either. Finally, the halting language separates recognizable from decidable languages, so not every recursively enumerable language is recursive.

For a fixed valid word w of length n, a DFA for strings ending in w needs n+1 states representing the longest consumed suffix that is a prefix of w. A CFG is ambiguous when some word has two distinct parse trees, equivalently two different leftmost derivations. Different expansion orders that give the same tree do not prove ambiguity.

Separate precedence levels: E→E+T|T, T→T*F|F, F→id|(E). Multiplication binds inside T before addition at E, and left recursion encodes left association. Uniqueness follows by the top-level last operator split and induction. S→SS|ε is already ambiguous for ε. S→A|B is ambiguous if A→ab and B→abB|ε both produce ab. Ambiguous grammar and inherently ambiguous language differ: another grammar may remove ambiguity.

answer_review.explanation: In C, F generates id, T is a nonempty sequence of Fs separated by ×, and E a nonempty sequence of Ts separated by +. The last + uniquely determines the top E→E+T split; each T is uniquely split at its last ×. Induction on operator count gives a unique parse. A allows different groupings of id-like operands through E+E and E*E. B already has two trees for ε: S→ε and S→SS→εε. D is also ambiguous: ab is generated by S→A→ab and S→B→abB→ab. Supporting assigned module PDF pages: 8, 8.

The left side therefore also belongs to V∪Σ and its string closure; alternatives stating these weaker memberships can all be true. A deterministic finite automaton (DFA) is M=(Q,Σ,δ,q₀,F), with finite nonempty Q, start q₀∈Q, accepting set F⊆Q and total δ:Q×Σ→Q. Exactly one next state is specified per state/symbol pair; this does not mean the whole machine has one transition.
A nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA) permits zero, one or many successors: δ:Q×Σ→𝒫(Q).
An NFA is not more expressive than a DFA: both recognize exactly REG. Nondeterminism can make a description smaller.

Complexity classes here contain decision languages. P consists of deterministic polynomial-time decidable languages; NP consists of nondeterministic polynomial-time decidable languages, equivalently polynomially verifiable yes-instances with polynomial-size certificates. A verifier must accept some certificate exactly for yes-inputs; no certificate may falsely establish a no-instance. NP means nondeterministic polynomial, not non-polynomial.

P⊆NP because a verifier can ignore its certificate and run the P algorithm. P=NP remains open; NP does not mean definitely hard or definitely outside P. Finding versus verifying is an intuition for witnesses, not a rule that all NP instances need exponential search.
X is NP-hard if every A∈NP satisfies A≤pX. It need not belong to NP and can even be undecidable. X is NP-complete if X∈NP and X is NP-hard.

evidence.quote: A deterministic finite automaton (DFA) is M=(Q,Σ,δ,q₀,F), with finite nonempty Q, start q₀∈Q, accepting set F⊆Q and total δ:Q×Σ→Q. Exactly one next state is specified per state/symbol pair; this does not mean the whole machine has one transition. F may be empty, recognizing ∅.

Start at q₀ and consume the entire input. Accept iff the ending state is in F; visiting an accepting state earlier is insufficient. ε is accepted exactly when q₀∈F. A nonaccepting sink loops on every symbol and cannot reach acceptance; it still finishes after finite input. Finite automata have finite memory encoded by states, not no state or no ability to remember any history.

evidence.quote: For a fixed valid word w of length n, a DFA for strings ending in w needs n+1 states representing the longest consumed suffix that is a prefix of w. Overlapping prefixes determine fallback transitions. Distinct prefixes are distinguishable by suitable continuations, proving the lower bound; do not add an unnecessary rejecting sink.
For strings starting with w, a complete DFA ordinarily has n matched-prefix stages, an accepting continuation state and a rejecting sink: n+2 when n≥1 and the alphabet allows mismatches.

evidence.quote: A nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA) permits zero, one or many successors: δ:Q×Σ→𝒫(Q). An ε-NFA additionally permits moves without consuming input, using domain Q×(Σ∪{ε}). Some books include ε moves in the term NFA; state the convention. An NFA accepts iff at least one finite path consumes the complete word and finishes in F, including permitted ε moves before/after symbols.
An NFA is not more expressive than a DFA: both recognize exactly REG. Nondeterminism can make a description smaller. A DFA is a special NFA after interpreting its unique successor as a singleton set.

evidence.quote: A nondeterministic pushdown automaton (PDA) adds a stack to finite control: (Q,Σ,Γ,δ,q₀,Z₀,F). Its transition relation maps (state,input symbol or ε,stack top) to possible (new state,replacement stack string) pairs.

A stack is last-in, first-out: push adds an item at the top and pop removes the top item, so the most recently pushed item is removed first. A PDA accesses this top rather than an arbitrary interior position.

A queue is first-in, first-out: insertion at the rear and removal at the front returns the oldest waiting item. A linked list can implement a storage discipline, but the implementation container is different from the abstract push/pop or enqueue/dequeue access rule.

evidence.quote: An off-line TM has a read-only input tape and separate read/write work tape. Multitape, multihead, two-way-infinite-tape and nondeterministic TMs have the same language-recognition power as standard TMs, though simulation costs differ. Two unbounded stacks can simulate a tape. Turing completeness means ability to simulate general TM computation, not polynomial speed or literally using infinitely many cells in a finite run. The Church–Turing thesis connects effective procedures to this formal model; it is not a proved runtime theorem.

evidence.quote: Complexity classes here contain decision languages. P consists of deterministic polynomial-time decidable languages; NP consists of nondeterministic polynomial-time decidable languages, equivalently polynomially verifiable yes-instances with polynomial-size certificates. A verifier must accept some certificate exactly for yes-inputs; no certificate may falsely establish a no-instance. NP means nondeterministic polynomial, not non-polynomial.

evidence.quote: Boolean satisfiability was the first problem proved NP-complete, through the Cook–Levin theorem. Its hardness proof starts directly from an arbitrary nondeterministic polynomial-time computation and constructs a Boolean formula that is satisfiable exactly when an accepting computation exists.

This starting point matters: once one NP-complete problem is available, later hardness proofs can reduce that known problem to a new target. Membership in NP remains a separate obligation. Checking a satisfying assignment is efficient; whether finding one is always polynomial-time remains unresolved.
SAT asks whether a Boolean formula has a satisfying assignment; Cook–Levin establishes SAT NP-complete. CNF-SAT and 3-SAT are NP-complete versions.

evidence.quote: Static checks occur before execution: type compatibility, duplicate declarations within a restricted scope, valid names, argument counts, return compatibility and control-flow placement. A break is valid only in constructs allowed by the language; in C/C++ it can exit a loop or switch. A compiler may annotate an AST or create typed IR; there is no mandatory uniquely named output tree.

Dynamic checks depend on runtime values, such as some bounds and null checks. Static analysis can prove some accesses safe or faulty; “all memory errors cannot be statically checked” is too strong. Unreachable code is not universally a semantic error: some languages reject it in specified cases, others merely warn or optimize it away.

evidence.quote: A syntax-directed definition is a CFG with attributes on grammar symbols and semantic rules on productions. An annotated parse tree displays computed attribute values; it is not itself an inherited or synthesized attribute. Synthesized attributes flow from children to a parent; inherited attributes carry context from parent or siblings.

For E→E1+T, E.val=E1.val+T.val synthesizes an expression value. A declaration’s type environment passed into its body is inherited. S-attributed definitions use only synthesized attributes and fit LR reduction-time evaluation naturally; suitable LL parsers can also compute them. L-attributed definitions restrict dependencies so a left-to-right traversal can evaluate inherited context. Attribute dependency cycles can prevent evaluation.

evidence.quote: Constant folding evaluates constant expressions during compilation: 3*4→12. Constant propagation substitutes known values: x=3; y=x+2 becomes y=3+2 before folding. Copy propagation substitutes a copied name while its source remains unchanged. Dead-code elimination removes unreachable code or computations whose values are unused and whose evaluation has no necessary side effects.

Common-subexpression elimination reuses an earlier value only if operand values and relevant memory remain unchanged. A DAG can represent sharing. Algebraic simplification removes identities when valid: integer x+0→x. Strength reduction replaces an operation with an equivalent cheaper form, such as unsigned x*8→x<<3 for a valid width and shift count. Target costs determine whether it is actually cheaper.

Peephole optimization examines short instruction windows. It can remove redundant loads/stores, replace machine idioms and shorten jump chains: jump L1 where L1 immediately jumps L2 can become jump L2. “Local optimization” is a wider category; peephole is a concrete method, so a question offering both must specify the level requested.

answer_review.explanation: Optimization changes intermediate code to remove inefficiencies (PDF p. 7). The module lists peephole transformations and constant propagation (p. 18), and elimination of never-executed or unreachable statements (p. 18). Each can improve an intermediate representation before target code is emitted; no exclusive ordering among those transformations is specified.

choices.explanation: Peephole transformation improves instruction sequences (p. 18).

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Constant propagation is a listed optimization technique (p. 18).

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Removing unreachable intermediate statements is dead code elimination (p. 18).

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: All three fit the optimization of intermediate code described on p. 7.

evidence.quote: A symbol table maps names or symbol identities to attributes: type, scope, width, storage offset, parameter signature, constant information or linkage. A hash table gives expected O(1) insertion/lookup with suitable hashing; a stack of scope tables supports lexical nesting. Search the nearest scope first, insert declarations in the current scope, and remove visibility when leaving it.

Scanning may intern a spelling first; semantic analysis determines the declaration and type. Implementations differ, so first interaction is conventional rather than universal. Not every punctuation token needs a symbol-table entry; literals may use a separate literal table. A hash table is an implementation, not the information’s semantic role.

evidence.quote: A syntax-directed definition is a CFG with attributes on grammar symbols and semantic rules on productions.

A syntax-directed translation scheme embeds executable actions in productions; the actions run while translating a source program, not while generating the compiler. Attributes may compute types, values, AST pointers or generated code.

A type checker verifies that operations are defined for their operands. In a simple strict language, integer mod requires two integers; array indexing requires an array and integer index; an if condition requires Boolean; assignment requires equal or convertible types. Function calls check parameter count and compatibility, and returns match result types.

answer_review.explanation: The compiler in the scenario evaluates type attributes and applies compatibility checks as grammar productions are processed. This is syntax-directed translation: semantic rules or actions are attached to grammatical structure. Pure lexical analysis only recognizes tokens, and pure syntax recognition alone does not establish operand-type compatibility. Optimization transforms an already analyzed representation. Parsing can invoke these semantic actions, so the mechanism is more precise than naming syntax analysis alone.

evidence.quote: A basic block is a maximal straight-line instruction sequence entered at its beginning and exited at its end. Leaders are the first instruction, every jump target, and each instruction after a branch. Start a block at each leader and continue until the next leader.

Immediate left recursion has A→Aα. For A→Aα|β, where β does not start with A, introduce a new nonterminal A′ and use:
A→βA′
A′→αA′|ε

A→αA′
A′→β|γ

evidence.quote: IR separates source analysis from target implementation, allowing optimizers and backends to be reused. It should be easy to generate, analyze, transform and lower.

evidence.quote: A token is a category with optional attribute, such as (ID, symbol-entry) or (INT_LITERAL,42). A lexeme is the actual character sequence, such as total or 42. A pattern specifies which lexemes belong to a token class. The scanner emits an ordered token stream, not an unordered mathematical set.

Keywords, identifiers, literals, operators and punctuation are token classes. Whitespace and comments are usually skipped while line/column positions are retained. In indentation-sensitive or newline-sensitive languages, layout can carry tokens. Parse-tree construction is a parser task; scanning can intern identifier spellings, but declaration scope and types need later analysis.

answer_review.answer_text: Lexeme is the source text; token is its category with optional attributes.
answer_review.hint: Identify each activity’s input and output. Distinguish character recognition, grammatical structure, semantic checks and target implementation.
answer_review.explanation: COMP04 directly distinguishes the actual character sequence from its token category and optional attribute. For example, total is a lexeme that may produce an ID token associated with a symbol entry. Neither term is restricted to keywords; the same distinction applies to identifiers, numeric literals, operators and other lexical units.

evidence.quote: A value is live where it can be used before redefinition. In the interference model, values that must coexist in distinct registers are connected by an edge; each register is a color. Nonoverlapping live ranges may share a register. If a valid assignment cannot fit the available registers, spilling places selected values in memory and inserts loads/stores.

The general graph k-colorability decision problem is NP-complete for fixed k≥3; optimal register assignment/spill minimization is a hard optimization problem in general, so practical allocators use heuristics.

evidence.quote: Reaching definitions is forward may-analysis: which assignments can reach this point without a replacement definition? OUT=GEN∪(IN−KILL), with IN the union of predecessor OUT sets. Available expressions is usually forward must-analysis: an expression has been computed on every relevant path and its operands have not changed. Join with intersection.

answer_review.answer_text: Assignments that may reach a point without being overwritten.
answer_review.hint: Track which facts can hold along one path and which must hold along every path. Apply the specified direction, transfer rule and join operation.
answer_review.explanation: COMP29 directly defines reaching definitions as assignments that can arrive at a point without a replacement definition on the path. Its join is union because one possible path suffices. Liveness asks about future uses, available expressions asks about previous computations on every path, and possible call targets is a separate analysis question.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the exact assignment-and-no-overwrite property defined for reaching definitions.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Available expressions concerns prior computations with unchanged operands, not assignment definitions.

choices.label: D

evidence.quote: A basic block is a maximal straight-line instruction sequence entered at its beginning and exited at its end. Leaders are the first instruction, every jump target, and each instruction after a branch. Start a block at each leader and continue until the next leader.

A control-flow graph has blocks as vertices and possible next-block transfers as edges, including fall-through. A node D dominates N when every entry-to-N path passes through D. For an edge N→H where H dominates N, H is a loop header of a natural loop. This structure supports loop analysis. An expression DAG records value dependencies, not arbitrary control flow.

answer_review.answer_text: Every entry-to-N path passes through D.
answer_review.hint: Identify what the representation stores, what it omits and which later transformations it must support; separate a representation property from an algorithmic task.
answer_review.explanation: COMP28 defines domination relative to a particular node N: every path from entry to N must pass D. This is not a claim that D precedes every node in the program, nor is domination measured by out-degree or being a unique successor. The definition concerns unavoidable traversal on paths reaching the specified node.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The number of outgoing edges does not establish unavoidable traversal on paths.

choices.label: D

evidence.quote: SLR(1) uses LR(0) states and FOLLOW(A) for reduction by a completed A production. Canonical LR(1) attaches context-specific lookahead to items. LALR(1) merges canonical states with the same LR(0) core, combining lookaheads; merging can introduce reduce/reduce conflicts. The standard grammar-class hierarchy is LR(0)⊆SLR(1)⊆LALR(1)⊆LR(1), with increasing capability and often table size.

A shift/reduce conflict offers both consuming a token and reducing; reduce/reduce offers two reductions. An SLR or LALR conflict does not by itself prove the grammar ambiguous. Canonical LR(1) handles LR(1) grammars, not every unambiguous CFG. Precedence and associativity can resolve suitable expression conflicts; changing parser names alone does not repair all ambiguity.

answer_review.answer_text: FOLLOW(A), once the item for A→α is complete.
answer_review.hint: Use construction direction, lookahead and grammar restrictions. Distinguish algorithm families, implementations and coverage before comparing them.
answer_review.explanation: COMP17 says SLR uses LR(0) states and FOLLOW(A) for reduction by a completed A production. The completed item establishes that the right side has been recognized; FOLLOW restricts which lookaheads permit reducing it. FIRST information predicts beginnings instead, and FOLLOW of an arbitrary right-hand string is not the table rule used here.

evidence.quote: Static storage lasts throughout execution; stack frames support nested calls and recursion; heap storage supports lifetimes beyond a call. A frame may contain parameters, return address, saved registers, locals and temporaries. Sizes, alignment and offsets are target-dependent; a module’s two-byte int is an example, not a C++ guarantee.

A calling convention specifies argument and result locations, caller/callee-saved registers, stack alignment and frame responsibilities. Escape analysis asks whether an object/reference can outlive or be accessed outside a region such as its allocating call. Proven nonescaping allocations may use stack storage or be eliminated by scalar replacement, provided identity and lifetime semantics remain correct.

A proven nonescaping object may use stack storage or be eliminated when lifetime and identity are preserved. Bounds checking, exception reachability and pointer arithmetic are separate analyses and do not define the reference-escape property described.

evidence.quote: Inlining replaces a call with a suitably renamed copy of its body, preserving argument evaluation, returns and side effects. It can remove call overhead and expose optimization opportunities, but may increase code size and instruction-cache pressure. A recursive function cannot simply be expanded without limit.

Virtual dispatch chooses an overridden method based on a receiver’s runtime class. A common implementation uses a per-class virtual-method table and an object pointer to the table; the call loads the selected entry. This is an implementation strategy, not a universal language requirement. Name mangling distinguishes linker symbols, often for overloads; it is not itself runtime method selection. Proven receiver types may permit devirtualization.

answer_review.answer_text: A virtual method table (vtable) per class, with function pointers resolved at runtime
answer_review.hint: Match stored information to its lifetime, access path and calling-convention role; distinguish compile-time organization from run-time storage.
answer_review.explanation: A common implementation stores virtual-method entries in a per-class vtable and lets an object refer to the appropriate table. A virtual call selects the entry using the receiver’s runtime class. Static binding alone does not provide that selection for an unknown class. Mandatory inlining is not generally possible, and name mangling distinguishes linker symbols rather than selecting overrides at runtime.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Unknown runtime receivers prevent mandatory inlining of all polymorphic calls.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Name mangling identifies symbols rather than selecting overrides.

evidence.quote: A compiler translates a source program into an equivalent target representation while preserving defined observable behavior. The target may be machine code, assembly, bytecode or another source language. A transpiler is a source-to-source compiler, not a fundamentally separate noncompiler technology. A compiler preserves language semantics, not the programmer’s unstated intention.

An interpreter executes a program representation; it need not work one source line at a time. Systems can compile to bytecode and then interpret or JIT-compile it. AOT compilation happens before execution; JIT compilation happens during execution and may use runtime profiles. Neither is universally faster; startup cost, optimization and workload matter.

answer_review.answer_text: JIT compiles during execution; AOT compiles before execution.

The timing contrast in B is correct, while no universal speed guarantee, absence of optimization or restriction to interpreted languages follows.

evidence.quote: De Morgan gives (AB)'=A'+B' and (A+B)'=A'B'.

choices.explanation: NOT(A+B) is NOR and differs from NOT(A·B), for example when only one input is high.

evidence.quote: Useful identities are A+0=A, A·1=A, A+A=A, AA=A, A+A'=1, AA'=0, A+AB=A and A(A+B)=A.

answer_review.explanation: COA35 defines pipelining by overlapping stages from different instructions and says it primarily improves throughput. C directly states that mechanism. Pipeline fill/drain, stalls and the slowest stage constrain actual gains, so overlap rather than guaranteed latency reduction is the supported explanation.

In the conventional C++ toolchain: source → preprocessing → compilation proper → assembly → object files → linking → executable → loading → execution. Preprocessing handles directives such as #include; compilation may emit assembly; the assembler emits machine instructions in an object file. The linker resolves external symbols and combines object files and libraries. The loader places an executable and required components in memory and starts it.
Java javac produces bytecode, which a JVM interprets or compiles at runtime.

answer_review.answer_text: D. Native machine instructions in an object file
answer_review.hint: Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details.
answer_review.explanation: The specified native pipeline stops after the assembler produces an object file and before the linker combines objects and resolves external references. Its code is therefore native machine instructions in an object file. Machine-independent bytecode belongs to a different translation target, such as javac’s output, while a complete linked executable comes later in this C++ pipeline. Neither A nor B correctly names the specified result.

&& evaluates its right operand only if the left is true; || only if the left is false. Thus false && dangerousCall() skips the call. Bitwise & operates on bits and does not short circuit. With x=1,y=0,z=4, (x&y)||++z evaluates ++z, leaving z=5 and the Boolean result 1. The precedence ladder is grouping/postfix, unary, multiplicative, additive, shifts, relations, equality, bitwise &, ^, |, &&, ||, conditional, assignment, comma.

evidence.quote: Machine instructions are conventionally first generation; symbolic assembly is second; general high-level languages such as C++ and Java are third. Database query and application generators such as SQL are conventionally fourth generation. Fifth generation is a loose historical category associated with declarative logic, constraints and AI/expert systems. Generations do not determine whether an implementation uses an interpreter.

In the conventional C++ toolchain: source → preprocessing → compilation proper → assembly → object files → linking → executable → loading → execution. Preprocessing handles directives such as #include; compilation may emit assembly; the assembler emits machine instructions in an object file. The linker resolves external symbols and combines object files and libraries. The loader places an executable and required components in memory and starts it.

The added memory-write condition distinguishes the mechanisms without claiming every overflow executes code.

Multiplexing combines multiple input streams onto a shared link; demultiplexing separates them at the receiver. It differs from broadcasting one message to many destinations. FDM assigns distinct frequency bands with suitable guard spacing; WDM assigns different optical wavelengths. TDM allocates time slots: synchronous TDM reserves recurrent slots even if an input is idle, while statistical TDM allocates according to demand and needs identification.

Physical topology describes link layout; logical topology describes communication/access relationships. Point-to-point links join two endpoints; multipoint links share a medium. A full mesh consists of point-to-point links, correcting the module’s contradictory mesh statement.

Simplex is one way, half duplex alternates directions, and full duplex permits simultaneous sending/receiving. A walkie-talkie is half duplex; a telephone conversation uses full duplex. Serial sends sequential bits; parallel uses multiple conductors and may suffer skew. Character-oriented asynchronous serial adds start/stop bits; synchronous framing uses ongoing clock recovery. Neither is synonymous with browser asynchronous requests.

evidence.quote: Random access allows contention: ALOHA sends opportunistically; CSMA senses before sending. In legacy half-duplex Ethernet, CSMA/CD detects collision, sends a jam indication, stops, and retries after random backoff. The jam signals a collision, not its clearance. Wi-Fi 802.11 uses CSMA/CA with waiting/backoff and acknowledgments; sensing does not eliminate hidden-terminal collisions.

Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.

evidence.quote: Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.

evidence.quote: Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.

Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.

evidence.quote: HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.

Usual service ports: FTP control 21, SSH 22, Telnet 23, SMTP relay 25, DNS 53, HTTP 80, POP3 110, IMAP 143, HTTPS 443. Telnet provides unencrypted remote terminals; SSH protects remote access. Servers can be configured on other ports. A browser’s HTTP exchange does not determine the physical duplex mode of its network interface.

HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.

Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.

DNS resolves names to records, including IPv4 A and IPv6 AAAA addresses; it can use UDP or TCP port 53. DHCP dynamically leases IPv4 settings, commonly address, mask, gateway and DNS server. Its basic exchange is discover, offer, request, acknowledge. IP itself does not assign addresses.

ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 next hop to a link address, using a broadcast request and normally unicast reply. For an off-subnet target, ARP resolves the gateway, not the remote target’s MAC. These are separate companion protocols, not four pieces whose combination is IP.

Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.

Random access allows contention: ALOHA sends opportunistically; CSMA senses before sending. In legacy half-duplex Ethernet, CSMA/CD detects collision, sends a jam indication, stops, and retries after random backoff. The jam signals a collision, not its clearance. Wi-Fi 802.11 uses CSMA/CA with waiting/backoff and acknowledgments; sensing does not eliminate hidden-terminal collisions.

TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.

IP supplies connectionless best-effort packet delivery, not end-to-end ordering or retransmission. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits. Its minimum header is 20 bytes and can grow to 60 bytes; it is not a 32-bit header. IHL counts 32-bit words; total length includes header and payload. TTL limits lifetime across routers; the protocol field identifies TCP, UDP or another upper-layer protocol.

Simplex is one way, half duplex alternates directions, and full duplex permits simultaneous sending/receiving. A walkie-talkie is half duplex; a telephone conversation uses full duplex. Serial sends sequential bits; parallel uses multiple conductors and may suffer skew. Character-oriented asynchronous serial adds start/stop bits; synchronous framing uses ongoing clock recovery. Neither is synonymous with browser asynchronous requests.

Transmission delay is packet bits divided by link bit rate; propagation delay is distance divided by signal speed. Processing and queueing add delay. A 1000-byte packet takes 0.8 ms to serialize at 10 Mbit/s; increasing line rate does not reduce propagation time.

A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A VPN, Virtual Private Network, provides a logical private connection over another network; a secure VPN authenticates/encrypts its tunnel. A modem modulates outgoing and demodulates incoming carrier signals. These functions may coexist in one home router but remain conceptually distinct.

Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.

Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.

evidence.quote: The four-layer TCP/IP model folds OSI layers 5–7 into application, retains transport, calls layer 3 Internet, and combines link/physical as network access. A model is a guide to functions, not a guarantee that every application gets a reliable network. evidence.quote: ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 next hop to a link address, using a broadcast request and normally unicast reply. For an off-subnet target, ARP resolves the gateway, not the remote target’s MAC. It bridges the network/link addressing boundary and is often classified at the link layer; a bank calling ARP simply a network protocol uses a loose textbook convention. RARP reverses hardware-to-IP lookup; BOOTP/DHCP support boot configuration. ICMP reports errors and diagnostics; IGMP manages IPv4 multicast membership. These are separate companion protocols, not four pieces whose combination is IP.

HTTP defines web request/response semantics; it is stateless, and a message body may be absent. HTTPS adds TLS protection. FTP transfers files using control and separate data connections; it is not the same protocol as SFTP. SMTP submits and relays mail; POP3 retrieves messages and IMAP accesses/synchronizes server mailboxes. Saying SMTP handles both sending and end-user mailbox retrieval is inaccurate.

TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.

A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A VPN, Virtual Private Network, provides a logical private connection over another network; a secure VPN authenticates/encrypts its tunnel. A modem modulates outgoing and demodulates incoming carrier signals. These functions may coexist in one home router but remain conceptually distinct.

ASK varies carrier amplitude, FSK frequency, PSK phase; QAM combines amplitude and phase. AM/FM/PM can carry analog data. PCM digitizes analog input by sampling, quantizing and encoding. Sampling must exceed twice the highest retained baseband frequency in practical designs; b-bit samples have 2^b quantization levels and uncompressed rate fs×b. PAM/PWM are pulse modulation methods; pulse amplitude or width alone is not a binary PCM code.

Line coding maps digital bits to digital signal patterns. NRZ uses levels without a forced mid-bit return; Manchester supplies a mid-bit transition for clocking, with bit convention specified. Differential Manchester encodes using transitions relative to previous state. AMI alternates the polarity of successive ones; pseudoternary alternates zero pulses. Block coding adds code redundancy; scrambling replaces problematic patterns without necessarily increasing bit count. Multilevel schemes include 2B1Q and 8B6T; MLT-3 uses a sequence of voltage transitions.

A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A VPN, Virtual Private Network, provides a logical private connection over another network; a secure VPN authenticates/encrypts its tunnel. A modem modulates outgoing and demodulates incoming carrier signals. These functions may coexist in one home router but remain conceptually distinct.

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.

evidence.quote: Data are raw representations; information is data interpreted for a purpose. Communication requires a message, sender, receiver, medium and agreed protocol. A source creates data; a transmitter converts it to a signal; a receiver reconstructs data. Distance affects engineering but is not a sixth component.

Transmission delay is packet bits divided by link bit rate; propagation delay is distance divided by signal speed. Processing and queueing add delay. A 1000-byte packet takes 0.8 ms to serialize at 10 Mbit/s; increasing line rate does not reduce propagation time.

evidence.quote: Physical topology describes link layout; logical topology describes communication/access relationships. Point-to-point links join two endpoints; multipoint links share a medium. A full mesh consists of point-to-point links, correcting the module’s contradictory mesh statement.

Bus uses a shared backbone; an unterminated break can disrupt the segment. Star connects endpoints through a central device: one edge failure isolates that endpoint, whereas central failure affects the star. Ring forms a loop; basic single rings are vulnerable to a break, while protected dual rings differ. Token passing is associated with Token Ring but is an access method, not a necessary property of every ring. Tree is hierarchical; hybrid combines arrangements.

evidence.quote: Sending proceeds from application data to transport segment/datagram, network packet, link frame and physical bits/symbols; receiving reverses the order. Each layer serves the layer above. A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.

TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, retransmission and windows. Flow control protects the receiver; congestion control protects network capacity. UDP sends independent datagrams with ports and a checksum but no built-in setup, delivery guarantee, retransmission or ordering. Live interactive traffic may choose UDP when late data is less useful than lost data. Application protocols can add reliability over UDP.

Twisted pairs reduce coupled interference; UTP has no added shield and STP adds shielding. Coax has an inner conductor and outer shield sharing an axis. Fiber guides light and resists electromagnetic interference; it supports high capacity and long reach, but requires suitable optics and installation. Exact speed, cost and reach depend on the specification, not the material alone. Fiber can still be tapped.

Radio, microwave and infrared are unguided media. Ground waves follow Earth, sky waves can reflect from ionized layers, and line-of-sight paths require suitable visibility. Microwaves are radio waves in the broader physical classification. Infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Directionality depends on antennas: omnidirectional means broad azimuth coverage, not equal radiation in every 3-D direction. Legacy Ethernet straight-through cables join unlike MDI/MDI-X roles; crossover joins like roles, such as PC–PC or switch–switch. Auto-MDI-X can remove that requirement.

evidence.quote: Analog signals vary continuously; digital signals use discrete symbol states. Data and signal types are separate: digital bits can modulate an analog carrier. A sine wave has amplitude, frequency and phase. Frequency f counts cycles/second, period T=1/f, and wavelength λ=v/f depends on propagation speed v. Phase specifies displacement within a cycle. Composite signals combine frequencies.

Line coding maps digital bits to digital signal patterns. NRZ uses levels without a forced mid-bit return; Manchester supplies a mid-bit transition for clocking, with bit convention specified. Differential Manchester encodes using transitions relative to previous state. AMI alternates the polarity of successive ones; pseudoternary alternates zero pulses. Block coding adds code redundancy; scrambling replaces problematic patterns without necessarily increasing bit count. Multilevel schemes include 2B1Q and 8B6T; MLT-3 uses a sequence of voltage transitions.

Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.

A firewall allows, rejects or inspects traffic under a security policy; it does not necessarily encrypt. A VPN, Virtual Private Network, provides a logical private connection over another network; a secure VPN authenticates/encrypts its tunnel. A modem modulates outgoing and demodulates incoming carrier signals. These functions may coexist in one home router but remain conceptually distinct.

answer_review.explanation: NET11 says routers forward IP packets between networks and separate broadcast domains. Accordingly internetwork communication and packet forwarding/switching describe routing, whereas ordinary local link broadcasts are not propagated across routers. Packet filtering can accompany the traffic-control function, so A is the normal-function exception, not a claim that no specially configured broadcast relay can exist.

evidence.quote: Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. evidence.quote: Multiplexing combines multiple input streams onto a shared link; demultiplexing separates them at the receiver. It differs from broadcasting one message to many destinations. FDM assigns distinct frequency bands with suitable guard spacing; WDM assigns different optical wavelengths. TDM allocates time slots: synchronous TDM reserves recurrent slots even if an input is idle, while statistical TDM allocates according to demand and needs identification.

Flooding sends copies on eligible outgoing links with duplicate/lifetime controls; random walk picks a neighbor probabilistically. Unicast targets one destination, broadcast all in a scope, multicast a subscribed group and anycast one member sharing an address, normally nearest under routing metrics. Multi-destination packets can list multiple targets; this is not necessarily identical to broadcast. Group multicast trees use mechanisms such as reverse-path checks; Ethernet spanning tree is a different layer-2 mechanism.

Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.

evidence.quote: Radio, microwave and infrared are unguided media. Ground waves follow Earth, sky waves can reflect from ionized layers, and line-of-sight paths require suitable visibility. Microwaves are radio waves in the broader physical classification. Infrared generally does not penetrate walls. Directionality depends on antennas: omnidirectional means broad azimuth coverage, not equal radiation in every 3-D direction. Legacy Ethernet straight-through cables join unlike MDI/MDI-X roles; crossover joins like roles, such as PC–PC or switch–switch. Auto-MDI-X can remove that requirement.

Attenuation reduces signal strength. Distortion changes shape, often because frequencies have different delays. Noise adds unwanted energy: thermal noise comes from random thermal motion, crosstalk leaks from nearby channels, and impulse noise is a short disturbance. Amplifiers amplify noise too; digital repeaters regenerate decisions but cannot reconstruct every corrupted bit.

evidence.quote: A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.

Each switch port separates collision domains; full-duplex point-to-point Ethernet has no collisions and does not use CSMA/CD. Switching permits independent conversations simultaneously. Broadcasts still reach the VLAN unless another control filters them. A layer-3 switch also routes, so device marketing names do not override the function being examined.

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.

NIC expands to Network Interface Card. It is the host’s network interface, providing the connection through which the host sends and receives network signals. A cable connector attaches the medium to that interface; it is distinct from an intermediary switch or router.

Routers forward IP packets between networks using destination prefixes and next hops. They separate broadcast domains and normally do not forward local link broadcasts. A default gateway is usually a router, while a protocol gateway can translate application formats; therefore a gateway is not inherently a device that implements every OSI layer.

A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses. An active hub is a multiport repeater: it repeats incoming signals onto other ports, placing half-duplex endpoints in one collision domain. A passive hub is a connector. A hub neither learns MAC addresses nor eliminates collisions. An endpoint such as a network printer consumes services; routers, hubs and access points are intermediary devices.

A bridge or ordinary Ethernet switch operates at layer 2. It learns source-MAC-to-port mappings, looks up the destination, forwards a known unicast to its port, filters it if the destination is on the incoming segment, and floods an unknown unicast or broadcast within its VLAN. A switch does not always send only to one destination port. Wireless access points normally bridge wireless and wired link-layer traffic.

Sending proceeds from application data to transport segment/datagram, network packet, link frame and physical bits/symbols; receiving reverses the order. Each layer serves the layer above. A router removes a received link frame, inspects IP, and creates a new link frame for the next hop. MAC addresses usually change across routed hops; end-to-end IP addresses ordinarily remain until translation.

Ports identify transport endpoints; the application can choose a transport and request socket buffer sizes, subject to OS limits. A TCP connection is identified by source/destination IP and source/destination port, with TCP understood. IPv4 protocol numbers identify upper protocols; 80 is a usual HTTP port, not an IP protocol number. Clients often use ephemeral ports. SCTP is a reliable message-oriented transport with multiple streams.

evidence.quote: ASK varies carrier amplitude, FSK frequency, PSK phase; QAM combines amplitude and phase. AM/FM/PM can carry analog data. PCM digitizes analog input by sampling, quantizing and encoding. Sampling must exceed twice the highest retained baseband frequency in practical designs; b-bit samples have 2^b quantization levels and uncompressed rate fs×b. PAM/PWM are pulse modulation methods; pulse amplitude or width alone is not a binary PCM code.

Analog signals vary continuously; digital signals use discrete symbol states. Data and signal types are separate: digital bits can modulate an analog carrier. A sine wave has amplitude, frequency and phase. Frequency f counts cycles/second, period T=1/f, and wavelength λ=v/f depends on propagation speed v. Phase specifies displacement within a cycle. Composite signals combine frequencies.

evidence.quote: CRC expands to Cyclic Redundancy Check.

Detection adds redundancy but does not guarantee correction. Even parity adds a bit so the total number of ones is even: 1011 needs parity 1. It detects every odd number of bit flips but misses even counts. CRC treats bits as a polynomial and appends the XOR-division remainder; the receiver repeats the division. Internet checksums add words with end-around carry and complement the sum. A burst spans from the first corrupted bit through the last, including unchanged interior bits. Retransmission or sufficient forward-error-correcting redundancy is needed for recovery.

evidence.quote: Circuit switching sets up a path with reserved resources, transfers data, then releases it. Predictable allocated bandwidth trades against setup/blocking and wasted reservation during silence. A traditional telephone call is the standard example. Packet switching divides data into packets that share links statistically; queueing can add variable delay and loss. This does not make modern voice-over-packet impossible: buffering, scheduling and capacity planning manage it.

Datagram packets are forwarded independently. Virtual circuits establish forwarding state, but resource reservation is optional, not a necessary property of every virtual circuit. Message switching stores a complete message before forwarding, without a dedicated end-to-end path. Packet store-and-forward waits for the full packet/frame; cut-through starts after enough header arrives; fragment-free historically waits through the initial collision-sensitive portion. No routing algorithm guarantees that every packet always takes the geometrically shortest route.

Controlled access uses polling, reservations or a token to grant turns; correctly coordinated access avoids contention collisions. Channelization divides frequency, time or code resources. Stop-and-wait sends one frame and waits for ACK, retransmitting on timeout; sequence bits distinguish duplicates. Sliding windows permit multiple unacknowledged frames. Link reliability/flow control is hop-local; transport reliability/flow control is end-to-end. Ethernet detects corruption but does not itself guarantee reliable delivery.

answer_review.explanation: NET31 defines packet store-and-forward as receiving the complete packet or frame before forwarding it. That is the switching principle named by B. Stop-and-wait is instead a reliability procedure that sends one frame and waits for acknowledgment. Cut-through alternatives exist, so the answer identifies the conventional principle without claiming every switch must use it.
