additions.title: Compilation versus operating-system execution services
paragraphs: A compiler translates source code toward an executable representation. For example, the conventional GCC toolchain distinguishes preprocessing, compilation proper, assembly and linking. A compiler uses operating-system services as a development tool; it is not the runtime kernel component that selects ready processes, manages memory or handles protected service requests.

sources.title: GCC — Options Controlling the Kind of Output

additions.title: Filesystem links in Linux
paragraphs: Linux provides link() to create another hard-link name for an existing file. The old and new names identify the same file, so hard links are not a Windows-only facility. unlink() removes a filesystem name; when that name is a symbolic link, it removes the link itself. Removing a name and erasing the target’s contents are different operations.

additions.title: Scope, understanding and changing requirements
paragraphs: Elicitation difficulties have several distinct sources. Scope problems concern agreeing on system boundaries and the appropriate level of detail. Understanding problems arise when stakeholders and analysts have different domain knowledge, omit tacit needs or communicate conflicting interpretations. Volatility means that requirements change as circumstances and understanding develop.
These difficulties call for repeated communication, explicit boundaries, negotiated meanings and controlled revision. They can occur together; resolving one does not automatically remove the others.

sources.title: CMU SEI — Issues in Requirements Elicitation

additions.title: Objects, shared models and specialization
paragraphs: An object-oriented approach can use a consistent vocabulary of objects, classes and relationships across analysis, design and implementation. Models are refined for different purposes rather than being identical artifacts. This continuity can reduce translation errors and effort; reusable classes can shorten suitable projects, but neither shorter duration nor good design is guaranteed.

Generalization places common concepts in a more general superclass and specialized concepts in subclasses. Available inherited attributes and operations are shared by subclasses, which may extend or override behavior. Defining common features once can reduce duplicated maintenance. The top of the hierarchy is more general, not more specialized.

Encapsulation groups state with operations and hides representation behind an interface. Polymorphism permits different object types to respond differently through a common operation or interface. Abstraction exposes the relevant contract while omitting unnecessary detail. Reusability means using suitable existing classes or components in new contexts rather than writing them again. These ideas support each other but name different properties.

additions.title: Modeling categories and data diagrams
paragraphs: In the course’s UML building-block terminology, structural things describe static conceptual or physical elements. Behavioral things describe dynamic interactions and state behavior. Grouping things organize model elements into packages. Annotational things attach explanatory remarks or constraints, usually as notes.

An entity–relationship diagram models entity types, their attributes and the relationships between them, commonly for data design. Its focus differs from a use-case diagram of external roles and goals, a class diagram of classes and their features, or a deployment diagram mapping artifacts to execution nodes.

additions.title: Plan-driven and adaptive planning
paragraphs: In a plan-driven process, activities are planned in advance and progress is assessed against that plan. Agile planning is incremental and adapts to changing needs. This distinction concerns planning strategy; a process can combine advance planning with staged deliveries and feedback.

additions.title: Exploration artifacts and collaborative implementation
paragraphs: A storyboard sketches a sequence of moments in a proposed interaction, helping people explore how a concept would be used. A wireframe sketches interface structure and the arrangement of content or controls. Both can inform requirements, but neither automatically supplies a complete use-case description with actors, preconditions, flows and postconditions.

Pair programming is a way for two programmers to work together on the same implementation task, commonly sharing a workstation with complementary writing and reviewing roles. It is an implementation collaboration practice rather than a replacement for modeling a user goal.

sources.title: IBM Enterprise Design Thinking Toolkit — Wireframes

additions.title: Distinguish a requirements specification from neighboring terms
paragraphs: A Software Requirements Specification records agreed software services and constraints. A Capability Development Document is a defense capability-requirements artifact describing needed capability characteristics and performance parameters; its specialized acquisition context differs from the ordinary software SRS. Domain-driven design is an approach that organizes software models around the business domain, not the name of an agreed requirements specification.

additions.title: Scalability and robustness are different qualities
paragraphs: Scalability is the ability to accommodate additional workload while maintaining the required service, often by increasing available resources. It concerns growth in demand. Compatibility concerns supported cooperating environments, such as browsers and devices; usability concerns successful and learnable user tasks.

Robustness concerns reliable operation across varied or difficult operating conditions and controlled failure outside the supported range. It is different from usability, which concerns people successfully learning and carrying out tasks. Improving an interface’s task success does not by itself establish robustness under adverse conditions.

additions.title: Java and JavaScript object-oriented models
paragraphs: Java organizes object-oriented programs using classes, objects, inheritance and interfaces. A class describes the state and behavior of its instances; inheritance relates a subclass to a superclass, and an interface specifies operations a type agrees to provide.

sources.title: Oracle Java Tutorials: Object-Oriented Programming Concepts

additions.title: Form values and result destinations
paragraphs: For a text input, the value attribute supplies its initial text value; it does not specify the control’s width. The type attribute selects the kind of input control.

A form’s target identifies the window or frame in which the submitted result is displayed. The action identifies the processing URL, so changing the destination context is different from changing the handler.

In an input element, type="text" creates text entry, type="checkbox" an independently selectable checkbox, type="radio" a radio choice, and type="submit" a submit button. A hidden input carries a value without displaying an editable text field; it is not a password-masking control.

additions.title: Message display versus response collection
paragraphs: alert(message), confirm(message) and prompt(message) all present a supplied message. Alert is a notification; confirm additionally asks for an OK/Cancel decision, while prompt additionally offers a text field. A general message-display description therefore differs from an information-only notification.

additions.title: Database API namespaces and affected rows
paragraphs: PDOStatement::rowCount() is a method on a PDO statement object that reports affected rows for its DELETE, INSERT or UPDATE statement. It is not a procedural MySQLi function, and its behavior for SELECT result counts is driver-dependent rather than a portable row-count guarantee.

With an initialized PDO connection, $pdo->query($sql) executes an SQL statement without placeholders and returns a PDOStatement for processing its results. The connection’s configured driver determines the database; the method name alone does not mean MySQL.
MySQL is an open-source SQL database management system. Its relational data-management role is distinct from the PHP API used to connect to it.

The procedural MySQLi query form is mysqli_query($conn, $sql), using a MySQLi connection and the correctly spelled function name. The pg_query function belongs to PHP’s PostgreSQL extension; it is not a MySQL connection API.

additions.title: JavaScript execution, statement forms and error categories
paragraphs: JavaScript implementations may interpret or compile source; interpretation and compilation are execution strategies rather than competing language identities.

An if statement conditionally executes code. The legacy with statement temporarily extends name lookup and is forbidden in strict mode. A debugger statement may invoke an active debugging facility. These are keyword-introduced statement forms, unlike the quoted use-strict directive.

A syntax error prevents source from being parsed successfully. A runtime error arises while executing a program. A logical error is a defect in the algorithm or expression that can produce an incorrect result without throwing an exception.

additions.title: PHP statement boundaries and string escapes
paragraphs: A complete ordinary PHP assignment statement ends with a semicolon. A string’s closing delimiter must match its opening delimiter; a single quote can appear inside a double-quoted string without ending it.

In double-quoted PHP strings, backslash-n represents a line feed and backslash-r represents a carriage return. The written sequences are \n and \r; forward-slash sequences such as /n are ordinary text. A backslash before a dollar sign preserves that dollar sign rather than starting variable interpolation.
The basic print and echo constructs can be written with or without parentheses when their syntax permits it. Parentheses do not add spaces or change the value of the emitted argument.

additions.title: Default text rendering and legacy frame fallbacks
paragraphs: In the browser’s default presentation, an i element typically displays its text in italics. This is a rendering convention: its text semantics are distinct from the stress emphasis represented by em, and CSS may override appearance.

A legacy frameset document could include noframes content for user agents that did not support frames or were configured not to display them. Frame support was therefore not universal even in that historical model.

additions.title: Numeric functions and NaN checks
paragraphs: For finite numeric arguments, Math.abs(x) gives the nonnegative magnitude, Math.floor(x) gives the greatest integer no larger than x, and Math.sqrt(x) gives the nonnegative square root for nonnegative x. These operations differ from ordinary nearest-integer rounding; floor moves toward negative infinity.

Global isNaN(value) tests whether conversion to Number produces NaN. Number.isNaN(value) tests specifically for the Number value NaN without coercion. NaN is itself a special numeric value, not a callable checking function.

additions.title: Destroying server-side session data
paragraphs: session_destroy() removes the data associated with the current PHP session. It does not itself unset every current script variable or delete the browser’s session cookie; destroying stored data, clearing $_SESSION and expiring the identifier cookie are separate parts of a complete logout.

additions.title: HTTP response status classes
paragraphs: The first digit of an HTTP status code identifies its class: 2xx means successful handling, 3xx means redirection or further action, 4xx indicates a client-error condition, and 5xx indicates a server-error condition. Classifying a code is different from identifying the precise condition represented by its last two digits.

additions.title: Authentication versus authorization
paragraphs: Authentication verifies a claimed identity. Authorization checks whether a particular entity is permitted to perform a requested action. Establishing identity does not grant every permission, and neither check alone repairs unsafe SQL construction or unsafe output encoding.

additions.title: Metadata purposes
paragraphs: The keywords metadata name supplies terms relevant to the page, while description supplies a page summary. Robots metadata supplies crawler indexing or search-presentation instructions. These roles differ from mobile viewport control.

sources.title: Google Search Central: Robots meta tag

additions.title: Remainder and logical conjunction
paragraphs: For nonnegative integers n and positive d, n % d gives the remainder after division; zero tests divisibility. With Boolean operands, && is true only when both operands are true; it is a logical operator, not a comment delimiter.

additions.title: Application protocols and underlying communication
paragraphs: HTTP defines web application requests, response status codes and representations. An HTTP exchange can use underlying TCP connections and IP addresses; naming that network stack does not identify the application-level method or status semantics.

FTP is a file-transfer application protocol. SMTP transports electronic mail. These service roles differ from the HTTP resource request/response semantics used by a web browser. HTTPS adds TLS protection to HTTP rather than replacing its resource semantics.

findings.issue: The repaired C key is correct, but the support row does not positively establish insertion sort’s fixed saved-element storage; DSA33’s statement that several sorts share constant storage does not identify insertion sort.

findings.issue: The C key and distinct-key reasoning are correct. Choice D’s completeness/last-level placement explanation is not taught by the quoted DSA23 paragraph, which calls the heap complete without defining that shape.
findings.recommended_fix: Add DSA18 and its existing exact passage “Complete means all earlier levels are filled and the last fills from left.” Include DSA23’s array-index rule if needed. Retain C; interpret D explicitly as the rightmost occupied position at the lowest level.

findings.issue: The clarified service-ADT reading supports A, but its only quotation teaches stack reversal. It does not supply the FIFO queue contrast or the linked-list-versus-service-interface distinction used to reject C.
findings.recommended_fix: Link DSA11, DSA14 and DSA45 with short existing passages on LIFO, FIFO, linked stacks and ADT versus representation. Keep A under the stated service-interface interpretation; do not describe a linked list as incapable of implementing reversal.

findings.issue: The main C answer and alternative-source B,C select-all answer are correct. The alternative’s insertion-sort contrast says it grows a sorted prefix, but variant_support lacks DSA34 and none of its quoted passages teaches that insertion step.
findings.recommended_fix: Add DSA34 to the S27 Q445 p193 variant_support and quote the existing initial-sorted-prefix/save/shift/insert rule. Union DSA34 into the main section_ids. Keep the variant’s explicit select-all stem and B,C labels.
